_comment: WHAT MAY BE ATTACHED TO THE ROADS (ADR-0420, docs/road-model-design.md section 1: 'every junction, street, lane
and connection has an id that never changes ... that is what lets anything else attach to the roads'). Each kind
says what it attaches to: 'street' (a street of the road model, at a station along it or the whole street),
'junction' (a junction as a whole), or 'arm' (one arm of a junction, which is also its street there). A kind
that names the street (its 'names' is true) is what a reader asks for when it wants a street's name. A kind with
'controls' stands only at a junction whose stated control is one of them (the rule sets' control kinds,
assets/scripts/rules/lab.lua; ADR-0421): the signal poles and heads stand where the control is 'signal'. The road
model refuses an attachment of a kind not listed here, or on the wrong thing. Adding a kind (a bus stop, a door)
is an entry here, not code.
A SIGN THAT FOLLOWS FROM A FACT (ADR-0424; docs/road-model-design.md, 'Placement policy'): a kind with a 'sign' row is
placed at load, one per arm the row's 'when' holds for, and attached to that arm. The row is the whole of the sign:
means            the rule set's device it stands for (assets/scripts/rules/lab.lua `devices`; absent: none -- a
one-way street is a fact of its lanes, not a device);
when             over STATED facts only: 'regulation' (the arm's stated signs, the junction's `arms[].regulations`),
'one_way_end' ('exit': a one-way street's traffic leaves it into the junction here; 'any': either
end), 'controls' (the junction's stated control is one of these; absent: any);
faces            whose traffic reads it: 'arriving' (by this arm), 'entering' (would enter this arm from the
junction), 'crossing' (arriving by each other arm that crosses this one: one sign each);
side             'kerb': on the kerb side of the traffic it faces; 'near_kerb_or_far_off': on the corner of this
arm nearest the reader when the arm is on the reader's kerb side, the far corner when it is on
their off side; two readers whose corners are one share its post, back to back;
else_side        'off': where the kerb side has no room, the same spot across the arm (a stated second place,
with its source; nothing is ever moved to fit);
from_stop_line   metres toward the junction from this arm's stop line (ADR-0419's rule: the widest other road at
its node's half width and 5.2 m back from where it meets the junction);
from_kerb        metres out onto the pavement from the kerb (the street's travel lanes and shoulder);
crossing_angle   (faces 'crossing') an arm within this many degrees of this arm's line, either way, does not cross it;
keeps_clear      metres from anything already standing there (signal poles, signs placed before it): a sign with
no room is not placed, and is reported; lamps, street trees and kerb props within it give way;
priority         placed in this order, lowest first (law and safety: 1 for a sign that stops or holds traffic);
look             the sign kit's request (assets/scripts/signs_us.lua): what it looks like; 'look_at' a junction
control's own look in its place; an 'arrow' of 'traffic': the street's direction as its reader
sees it;
source           where each choice comes from; '[~]' marks a guess to tune.
MUTCD below is the US Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices, 2009 edition (FHWA), read 2026-11-14 at
mutcd.fhwa.dot.gov through a page-summary tool (the paragraphs named were quoted back, not read line by line). Its
'right-hand side' is the kerb side where traffic keeps right; read here as the kerb side.

street_name.what: the street's name, stated in the road file (streets[].name), one per street of its run

name_sign.what: a street-name sign at a junction: one blade naming the arm's street (street_signs.h)

signal_pole.what: a traffic signal's pole on the kerb corner of the arm it governs (street_furniture.h)

signal_head.what: the signal head on that pole, facing the traffic arriving by the arm

street_lamp.what: a street lamp on the street's pavement, at a station along it

stop_sign.what: a STOP sign (R1-1) at an arm stated to stop, on its kerb, facing the traffic arriving by it

source: MUTCD 2B.10 para 01: on the near side of the junction, on the kerb side of the approach;
para 13: in advance of the crosswalk line nearest the approaching traffic -- 0.6 m past the stop line stands between it
and the crosswalk's near edge, 1.2 m apart in the paint (deck_mesh.h kCrosswalkNear..kStopLineBack) [~ the 0.6];
MUTCD 2B.05 para 04: an ALL WAY plaque (R1-3P) below each STOP sign where every approach stops;
MUTCD 2A.19 para 10: a lateral offset of at least 2 ft (0.6 m) where the usual one cannot be had (para 11: 1 ft from
the face of the kerb in business and residential areas)

give_way_sign.what: a YIELD sign (R1-2) at an arm stated to give way, on its kerb, facing the traffic arriving by it

source: MUTCD 2B.10 paras 01 and 14: as the STOP sign; the numbers as the STOP sign's [~ the 0.6]

do_not_enter_sign.what: a DO NOT ENTER sign (R5-1) at the exit end of a one-way street, facing traffic that would enter it the wrong way

source: MUTCD 2B.37 para 02: directly in view at the point where a road user could wrongly enter a one-way
roadway, on the kerb side of the roadway, facing traffic that might enter it the wrong way; para 05: a sign
on the other side may be used -- here only where the kerb side has no room (a divided road's narrow median)
[~ the 0.6: at the arm's stop line, as its STOP sign]

one_way_sign.what: a ONE WAY sign (R6-1) parallel to a one-way street where it meets a junction, facing each crossing approach

source: MUTCD 2B.40 para 02: parallel to the one-way street at every road that meets it; para 07: on the near
right and far left corners (near kerb side, far off side here), facing traffic entering or crossing it
(para 08, at signals: near the signal faces -- not done: the same corners) [~ the 3.0: at the corner,
clear of the stop and do-not-enter signs 0.6 m past the stop line; ~ the 30 degrees]

uses._comment: Which kind each reader writes or reads, so no reader names a kind in code.

_comment: The control the one-off tool states at a junction the old rule leaves dark (`lanes_tool controls`, ADR-0421):
the rule sets' word for no control. A lit junction gets the control signal_pole stands for.

map._comment: Each control's colour on the city map's junction layer (city_svg.h, ADR-0422).
